I will keep to the pattern I know best here in southern Hebei: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what fits my land, water, labor, and age. I am 70, so I will not take on crops that need too much hand work or risky market timing. Wheat and maize are steady, familiar, easy to sell, and match the local season well. At the start of this growing season, the winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage it through spring with one more topdressing, a few irrigations if water allows, and basic disease and insect control only when needed. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize on the same land so I do not lose soil moisture or time. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable yield and stronger resistance, not the trouble of saving my own seed. I will keep fertilizer moderate because input prices matter, and I will not chase very high yield. I will use rotary tillage before maize because it is easier for me than deep ploughing every season, while the wheat field was already prepared in the previous autumn with ploughing. I will irrigate mainly at the key stages and keep pesticide use limited, because I want to control cost and reduce unnecessary spraying.
